verdict.rationale: Sentry publishes self-hosted install docs claiming you can 'run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything' (sentry-docs-11, sentry-docs-26), and some long-term self-hosters report it running fine (sentry-comm-2). However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict the ease of this for local/dev use: the founder admits self-hosting is 'awful today' (sentry-comm-4), users report runaway container/memory growth even on 32GB servers (sentry-comm-5), and a database near-crash incident (sentry-comm-9) — suggesting spinning up and maintaining a dev instance is far heavier than implied. Missing for 10: dedicated lightweight dev-instance tooling (e.g., docker-compose quickstart optimized for testing), first-party guidance scoped to test/dev rather than production self-hosting, and independent confirmation that a minimal dev setup is trivial to spin up.
